QUOTE: "doxygen reads FILE_PATTERNS-matching files only + JS/TS via parse-built front end" and "The one content filter is `_drop_binary_files` (`filetypes.py`), which removes files that look binary from the first 8 KiB. Those paths are added to the exclude list so doxygen never opens them."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says scope enumeration isn't the whole story and names both the parse-built front end for JS/TS and the binary-file drop. The binary filter is described by content sniffing rather than as "extensions that lie", but it still names the mechanism.
